Our client is a leading UK organisation operating across multiple locations, supporting a large workforce within operational and customer-focused environments. Following a recent transformation of the HR function, the business has adopted a regional structure designed to provide a consistent, high-quality people service while creating greater opportunities for collaboration, development, and career progression.

The successful candidate will join a growing HR team based out of Hemel Hempstead, working closely with HR Business Partners and Employee Relations specialists who support multiple sites across the region. With a strong focus on operational excellence and continuous improvement, the organisation offers employees the chance to make a genuine impact while developing their careers within a supportive and evolving HR function.

Description

Reporting to the Regional HR Business Partner, the HR Coordinator will be based in Hemel Hempstead and provide comprehensive administrative support across the full employee lifecycle, ensuring HR processes are delivered accurately, efficiently, and in line with company policies.

Key responsibilities include:
- Managing HR administration from onboarding through to offboarding.
- Preparing contracts, employee correspondence, and HR documentation.
- Maintaining accurate employee records and ensuring data integrity within HR systems.
- Acting as a first point of contact for HR queries and escalating matters where appropriate.
- Supporting probation reviews, absence management processes, benefits administration, and other people processes.
- Coordinating onboarding activities, including documentation, compliance checks, and system setup.
- Monitoring shared HR inboxes and responding to employee and manager enquiries.
- Assisting with HR reporting, audits, and compliance activities.
- Supporting HR Business Partners and Employee Relations teams with projects and operational activity.
- Identifying opportunities to improve processes, systems, and ways of working.
- This role offers a blend of shared-services style HR administration and regional HR support, working with stakeholders across multiple sites while being primarily based in Hemel Hempstead. The position will suit someone who enjoys variety, takes ownership of their workload, and is comfortable working within a high-volume environment.

Profile

The successful candidate will have previous HR administration experience and be comfortable working within a busy, high-volume environment where accuracy and attention to detail are essential.

You may have experience in:
- HR Administration
- HR Shared Services
- HR Coordination
- People Administration
- Recruitment Administration
- Employee Lifecycle Administration

Experience gained within operational environments such as logistics, warehousing, distribution, manufacturing, retail, transport, or other blue-collar workforces would be highly advantageous.

The ideal candidate will demonstrate:
- Previous experience within an HR administrative or HR support role.
- Excellent attention to detail and strong organisational skills.
- Experience using HR systems and maintaining employee data.
- Confidence managing competing priorities and high volumes of work.
- A proactive approach to problem-solving and process improvement.
- Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.
- The ability to work independently while remaining a collaborative team player.
- A genuine interest in developing a long-term career within HR.

Part-qualified CIPD candidates are welcome to apply, and study support may be available for individuals looking to continue their professional development.
- Candidates should also be comfortable with a predominantly office-based role in Hemel Hempstead and enjoy building strong working relationships with colleagues and stakeholders in person.

Job Offer
- Competitive salary, negotiable dependent on experience
- Based in Hemel Hempstead with a predominantly office-based working model.
- Opportunity to join a newly structured and growing HR team.
- Clear progression opportunities into HR Advisor and broader generalist HR roles.
- Exposure to the full employee lifecycle within a large and complex organisation.
- Opportunity to develop specialist expertise in HR systems, compliance, process improvement, and people operations.
- Free on-site parking at the Hemel Hempstead office.
- 37.5-hour working week with flexibility around start and finish times.
- Immediate interview process with the opportunity to join the team as soon as possible.
- Excellent opportunity for candidates seeking a long-term HR career within a fast-paced operational business.

Location: Hemel Hempstead (ideally 5 days per week on site, with some flexibility considered for the right candidate).

title: Van Sales Administrator
description:
We are seeking a highly organised and detail oriented Van Sales Administrator to join our dynamic team. The successful candidate will play a vital role in supporting our van sales operation - retail, SME & Fleet, ensuring the accurate and efficient processing of sales orders, while maintaining high standards of compliance and documentation. Flexibility to work on an ad-hoc basis. Accuracy, and a proactive attitude are key attributes for this position.

Based in Welham Green, Hatfield the Sales Administrator will work closely with internal teams to ensure customer needs are met efficiently, from order through to delivery and beyond.

The role is office-based Monday to Friday, working hours 9.00am to 5.00pm.

Main Duties and Responsibilities:
- Order Processing: Accurately processing new and used vehicle orders, including amending specifications with the factory in Germany and building deals into internal systems for invoicing.

title: Receptionist
description: Are you a highly motivated, organised and flexible receptionist? If so, we are looking for a full-time Band 2 Receptionist to be based at the St Albans Health and Wellbeing Centre and Sandridge Gate Business Park, St Albans. We are seeking an experienced and motivated receptionist to work Monday - Friday, 9-5pm or 8.30-4.30pm depending on demand. The receptionist is the first point of contact for all patients, staff and visitors to these busy centres. This role requires travel between centres in St Albans and travel to Watford to cover for annual leave and sickness periods. HCT will prioritise recruitment of workers living in England under the new immigration rules for care workers effective from 9 April 2025. Employers must first prove that they have attempted to recruit a worker from within England who needs new sponsorship. This ensures that those who came to the UK to pursue a career in adult social care can do so. Applicants must have good organisational skills, a range of office skills and experience in working in reception/administration. Excellent customer service skills are essential, as you will have both face to face and telephone contact with service users on a daily basis. Good written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills, a friendly approach and being enthusiastic are all required for this post. A knowledge of SystmOne would be an advantage but not essential as training will be provided. Part of this role will require the successful applicant to be flexible to provide receptionist cover for holiday/sickness when required, this will involve travelling to other centres within the locality. A full valid driving licence and access to a car to use regularly for business purposes is essential (unless you have a disability as defined by the Equality Act 2010). To meet and greet all visitors/patients face to face at the centre, ensuring visitors and staff complete the signing in/out book. Checking patients in for appointments via our patient system (SystmOne). To deal with telephone enquiries. To ensure that all visitors/clients are dealt with in a professional and helpful manner. To be the first point of contact for the day-to-day administration of facilities operations. Manage the reporting of maintenance jobs. Be responsible for the security, appearance and general tidiness of reception including ensuring leaflets and posters around the centre are up to date and relevant to the service. Undertake other duties that may occur from time to time as directed by senior management. To manage room bookings, ensuring that the computerised system is updated and all clinical space is used as effectively as possible. To manage all incoming and outgoing post, liaising with courier drivers and other departmental staff as required. Maintain and update any contact details and instructions at the front desk. To be prepared to work at other Trust sites in an emergency and cover annual leave. Direct all patients and visitors to the correct waiting area. Deal with any incidents in the waiting/reception area (including the cleaning of spillages) and to keep the area tidy. Be responsible for monitoring stationery, stock and non-stock supplies and equipment. To record and receipt of supplies and manage rotation of stock orders. Please see attached Job Description for full details. The use of AI is monitored and if you have used it then you are required to declare this, as well as what type of AI tools you have used and for what purpose. We reserve the right to further test your individual knowledge and skills in relation to the requirements for the post through robust and thorough interview and assessment.

title: Administrator
description: Larksfield and Arlesey Medical Partnership is seeking a motivated and organised Administrator to join our friendly and supportive team. This is a varied role that provides essential administrative support across the practice, helping to ensure the efficient day-to-day running of services and supporting the delivery of safe, high-quality patient care. Working closely with the management team, clinicians and colleagues, you will contribute to a range of administrative functions while maintaining professionalism, confidentiality and excellent customer service he successful candidate will support safeguarding administration, manage incoming and outgoing correspondence, prepare meeting agendas and minutes, maintain safeguarding registers and action logs, and respond to administrative queries. The role also includes supporting the Rota Manager with clinician rota coordination, maintaining accurate records and clinical rotas, producing reports and documentation, and assisting with governance, quality improvement and CQC compliance activities. You may also provide administrative support to the reception and secretarial teams during periods of operational demand. Provide comprehensive administrative support across the practice. Support safeguarding administration, including maintaining safeguarding registers, trackers and action logs. Process safeguarding correspondence, referrals and information requests. Prepare meeting agendas, take accurate minutes and circulate actions. Monitor shared email inboxes and ensure correspondence is actioned appropriately. Respond professionally to administrative queries from patients, staff and external organisations. Escalate urgent clinical, safeguarding or operational concerns where appropriate. Support the Rota Manager with booking locum clinicians and maintaining clinical rotas. Ensure clinician sessions and rota changes are accurately recorded and communicated. Maintain accurate electronic records, spreadsheets and filing systems. Produce reports, letters and other administrative documentation. Support audits, searches and governance activities, including CQC evidence gathering. Work collaboratively with clinicians, reception, secretarial teams and external stakeholders. Maintain confidentiality and comply with all practice policies, information governance and safeguarding procedures. Provide additional administrative support across departments during periods of increased operational demand.
